title: What does EscrowFinish do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of EscrowFinish and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, EscrowFinish releases an existing escrow to its predetermined recipient when the escrow's release conditions are satisfied. [1]

A conditional escrow needs the matching fulfillment, and time restrictions still apply. The finishing account does not choose a replacement destination. Conditional fulfillment increases transaction cost relative to a simple payment. Inspect the validated finish and original escrow together; a published secret by itself is not proof that release succeeded. [1]

The EscrowFinish reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using EscrowFinish, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
